project-trajectory/scripts/baseline_snap.contract: baseline_snapshot.py: the `last_approved` baseline. copy_live(root, seed=False) -> paths written; byte-for-byte mirror of SNAPSHOTTED into docs/archive/last_approved/; stale carriers deleted; SystemExit without seed=True. load_all(root) -> {(stem, id col): {id: row}}; None when absent; RAISES on an unparseable file; rows_for collapses that None to {}. exists(root) -> bool; stamp(root) -> (rev, date); is_drifted / drifted_cells -> approved cells only; unanchored_findings -> advisory strings.
project-trajectory/scripts/baseline_snap.notes: Design of record: docs/plans/2026-08-15-baseline-snapshot-design.md. THE REFUSALS ARE THE CONTRACT, and each replaces a convenient degrade. The first snapshot blesses whatever text is in the tree, so it must ride the owner's reviewed signing commit: copy_live will not CREATE the directory, and --seed is reachable only from `intake.py snapshot --seed`. None and {} are opposite claims and the empty one reads as "re-bless everything with no diff shown", which is why an unparseable file raises and rows_for is the ONE place the sentinel collapses. The copy preserves repo-relative paths under the snapshot root, so `snapshot_root / rel` reuses every existing resolver verbatim. COUNTERPART IS intake, THE WRITER: exactly two callers of copy_live are sanctioned (intake._apply_flips, after the status write, and `intake.py snapshot`), and nothing may wire the copy into a freshness step — the snapshot is deliberately behind live whenever an amendment is pending, and that lag IS the signal. OWNER is the DESIGN row, not SR-140, on the Q1 polymorphism: SR-140 states the obligation and is answerable for both halves of it, while this row is one module's concrete surface. PROVISIONAL, for the review sitting to overturn.

project-trajectory/scripts/adjudicate_br.contract: The adjudicator-brief seam the session engine composes from: `compose(root, row, verdict_path, prompt_templates) -> (text, None) | (None, reason)`, selected by the row's DECLARED `Brief` cell rather than inferred from `SpecRef` (that inference is ambiguous - an amended test-case row and a red-TC census row carry the same one). The seam is ALL-OR-NOTHING and that is its whole contract: every assembler fills its template's slots from a real derivation or returns a reason, so the caller never receives a partially-filled judge's brief. What the caller owes in return is the fail-closed half - a row that DECLARES a brief this seam cannot compose must be held for a human, never dispatched with the worker assignment, because a judge briefed as a builder ends its session DONE like any other and the miss is silent.
project-trajectory/scripts/adjudicate_br.notes: intra-component (both CMP-008), declared because the fail-closed obligation lives on the CALLER and would otherwise be recorded nowhere. `ROUTED` names the briefs with an assembler today; `conflict` and `amendment` are deliberately absent, each with its missing derivation named in the module header.
